summary: Every input node affects a frequency and must be read, establishing a linear lower bound that the one-pass counting solution meets.

optimality.argument: Changing the value of any unread node can alter one or two required output frequencies, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n nodes. Expected constant-time hash updates count them in one traversal, and constructing the k-node result adds O(k), which is bounded by O(n).

replacement_checks.evidence: An uninspected node can be changed to a new or existing value and thereby change the required frequency multiset.
The reference performs one expected O(1) dictionary update per input node and creates exactly one result node per distinct value.
Authored cases cover one node, one repeated value, all-distinct values, maximum node values, tied frequencies, and several different count groups.
